name: FLOOR
description: FLOOR rounds a number down, toward negative infinity, to the nearest multiple of a specified significance.
tldr: Rounds a number down to the nearest multiple of significance.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The value you want to round.

parameters.name: significance
parameters.description: The multiple to which you want to round. In classic FLOOR, number and significance should share the same sign.

basicExample.description: Round 3.7 down to the nearest integer
basicExample.explanation: 3 is the largest multiple of 1 that is less than or equal to 3.7.

advancedExamples.title: Negative numbers round away from zero
advancedExamples.description: FLOOR rounds toward negative infinity, so negatives move away from zero.
advancedExamples.explanation: The largest multiple of 1 that is ≤ -3.7 is -4.

advancedExamples.title: Round to two decimal places
advancedExamples.scenario: Trim a value to the nearest 0.01.
advancedExamples.explanation: 123.45 is the multiple of 0.01 just below 123.456.

howItWorks: FLOOR finds the greatest multiple of significance that is less than or equal to number (rounding toward negative infinity). In the classic version, if number is positive and significance is negative, Excel returns #NUM!; FLOOR.MATH lifts that restriction.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: If number is positive and significance is negative, classic FLOOR returns #NUM! (FLOOR.MATH does not).
FLOOR rounds toward negative infinity, so negative numbers move away from zero.

commonErrors.cause: Number is positive while significance is negative (classic FLOOR).
commonErrors.fix: Match the signs, or switch to FLOOR.MATH.
Use numeric values or numeric references.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports FLOOR with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: How is FLOOR different from FLOOR.MATH?
faq.answer: FLOOR.MATH (Excel 2013+) allows any sign combination and adds a mode argument for negative rounding; classic FLOOR is stricter about signs.

faq.question: Why does FLOOR(-3.7, 1) equal -4?
faq.answer: FLOOR rounds toward negative infinity, so negatives go to the next lower integer (-4).
